title: Persistent Pulmonary Hypertension of the Newborn (PPHN)
subject: ss-paediatric-cardiology

steps.say: At birth, lung expansion and alveolar oxygenation trigger a swift decline in pulmonary vascular resistance, which is disrupted in persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn.
steps.tx: Understanding **PPHN pathophysiology** is essential for neonatal intensive care. Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn results from failure of normal postnatal drop in pulmonary vascular resistance, causing right-to-left extrapulmonary shunting across the patent ductus arteriosus and foramen ovale, precipitating refractory cyanosis. Comprehensive evaluation and serial clinical assessments remain essential to guide individualized management and ensure optimal patient outcomes.

steps.say: Clinicians confirm ductal-level right-to-left shunting by simultaneously comparing pre-ductal and post-ductal pulse oximetry or arterial blood gas tensions.
steps.tx: Establishing the **pre- and post-ductal saturation gradient** confirms clinical suspicion. A right radial (pre-ductal) to lower limb (post-ductal) arterial oxygen saturation difference greater than **10%** confirms ductal right-to-left shunting, documenting extrapulmonary diversion of deoxygenated blood into the descending thoracic aorta. Comprehensive evaluation and serial clinical assessments remain essential to guide individualized management and ensure optimal patient outcomes.

rows: Reflects blood perfusing the brain before ductal mixing
Demonstrates deoxygenation from ductal right-to-left shunt
Diagnostic confirmation of ductal right-to-left extrapulmonary shunting

steps.say: Differentiating cyanotic structural congenital heart defects from parenchymal lung pathology or PPHN relies on the standardised hyperoxia challenge.
steps.tx: The **hyperoxia test** differentiates cardiac from pulmonary pathology. In the hyperoxia test with **100%** inspired oxygen, PaO2 remaining below **100 mmHg** suggests cyanotic congenital heart disease rather than parenchymal lung disease, necessitating emergent echocardiographic evaluation to rule out transposition or total anomalous connections.

left.title: Parenchymal Pulmonary Disease
points: PaO2 typically rises above 150 mmHg on 100% inspired oxygen
Alveolar recruitment improves gas exchange across alveolar capillary barrier
Responsive to continuous positive airway pressure or surfactant replacement

right.title: Cyanotic CHD or Severe PPHN
points: PaO2 remains persistently below 100 mmHg despite 100% inspired oxygen
Extrapulmonary or intracardiac right-to-left shunting bypasses ventilated lungs
Mandates urgent bedside echocardiography to delineate structural defects

steps.say: Inhaled nitric oxide serves as the selective first-line pulmonary vasodilator by diffusing directly into vascular smooth muscle to activate soluble guanylyl cyclase.
steps.tx: Therapy with **inhaled nitric oxide** provides targeted selective relief. Inhaled nitric oxide at **20 ppm** is the specific first-line pulmonary vasodilator for term and late preterm neonates with refractory hypoxemia and **oxygenation index** exceeding **25**, relaxing pulmonary arterioles without compromising systemic arterial vascular resistance.

nodes.label: Inhaled nitric oxide (20 ppm) delivered via mechanical ventilator circuit
Diffuses selectively across ventilated alveolar-capillary membranes into smooth muscle
Stimulates soluble guanylyl cyclase to produce cyclic GMP
Promotes selective pulmonary vasodilation without causing systemic arterial hypotension

steps.say: The oxygenation index quantitatively grades the severity of hypoxic respiratory failure and directs escalation to pulmonary vasodilators or mechanical circulatory support.
steps.tx: Calculating the **oxygenation index** guides therapeutic escalation in neonatal respiratory failure. Oxygenation index is calculated as Mean Airway Pressure multiplied by FiO2 multiplied by **100** divided by post-ductal PaO2. Values exceeding 25 mandate pulmonary vasodilators, while sustained elevations herald life-threatening refractory hypoxemia requiring urgent consideration of advanced rescue modalities.

rows: Selective cGMP stimulation via guanylyl cyclase
First-line therapy at 20 ppm for oxygenation index >25
Augments and sustains cGMP-mediated pulmonary vasodilation
Inodilator improving RV contractility and lowering pulmonary afterload

steps.say: When inhaled nitric oxide is unavailable or produces an incomplete response, targeted inhibition of cyclic nucleotide breakdown provides vital adjuvant vasodilation.
steps.tx: Administering **sildenafil in neonates** provides vital adjuvant vasodilation in difficult-to-treat situations. Oral or intravenous **sildenafil** selectively inhibits phosphodiesterase-5 to augment cyclic GMP-mediated pulmonary vasodilation in PPHN, facilitating successful weaning from inhaled nitric oxide and preventing rebound pulmonary vasoconstriction in critically ill newborns managed in neonatal intensive care units.

left.title: Sildenafil Mechanism
points: Prevents enzymatic breakdown of intracellular cyclic GMP
Sustains nitric oxide-mediated pulmonary vascular relaxation

right.title: Clinical Application in PPHN
points: Available in both oral and intravenous formulations for neonates
Facilitates weaning from inhaled nitric oxide therapy
Provides crucial first-line therapy when nitric oxide is unavailable

steps.say: Intravenous milrinone uniquely provides inotropic support to the overloaded right ventricle while simultaneously lowering pulmonary vascular resistance.
steps.tx: The inodilator **milrinone** addresses right ventricular strain and afterload elevation. Intravenous **milrinone** provides phosphodiesterase-3 inhibition to improve right ventricular function and reduce pulmonary arterial afterload, augmenting stroke volume and lusitropy while requiring adequate intravascular volume resuscitation to prevent systemic arterial hypotension during continuous infusions.

left.title: Milrinone Hemodynamic Benefits
points: Phosphodiesterase-3 inhibition augments myocardial cyclic AMP
Improves right ventricular contractility and diastolic lusitropy
Reduces pulmonary vascular impedance to alleviate ventricular strain

right.title: Clinical Cautions & Requirements
points: Causes systemic vasodilation that may precipitate arterial hypotension
Mandates adequate intravascular volume loading before initiation
Avoid rapid loading boluses in hemodynamically unstable neonates

steps.say: When maximal medical pharmacotherapy and high-frequency ventilation fail to arrest progressive hypoxemic decompensation, extracorporeal life support offers a life-saving rescue.
steps.tx: Fulfilling neonatal **ECMO criteria** triggers mechanical circulatory rescue. Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation is indicated when **oxygenation index** exceeds **40** despite maximal medical therapy including inhaled nitric oxide, high-frequency oscillatory ventilation, and inotropes, achieving survival rates above 70-80% in reversible pulmonary vascular disease. Comprehensive evaluation and serial clinical assessments remain essential to guide individualized management and ensure optimal patient outcomes.
